12.head: 717eb58ec018a4c6f09a07e9d52e8920706d618b
12.feedback: {"head":"717eb58ec018a4c6f09a07e9d52e8920706d618b","verdict":"pass","summary":"The change adds a Node-only, read-only reporter (scripts/factory/diagnostics.cjs) invoked only on a failed Claude model step, which builds a bounded, allowlist-only JSON report (fixed tool names, fixed command categories/forms, counts, stop reason) from the pinned action's temporary execution file and uploads it under a separate \"diagnostic-<phase>-<grantId>\" artifact name with 7-day retention. Verified against the current source: the reporter is copied into $RUNNER_TEMP/factory-control before the untrusted ticket head is checked out (same trust boundary already used for worker.cjs), so it cannot be tampered with by ticket/repo content. It correctly distinguishes \"denials array present but empty\" (status=available, denialCount=0) from \"denials missing/invalid\" (status=unavailable, denialCount=null, explicit reason) — never fabricating a zero. File reads are bounded (8 MiB, re-checked after fstat to avoid TOCTOU growth), symlinks/directories are rejected via lstat+O_NOFOLLOW, and the output file is written with O_EXCL so a pre-existing file is refused rather than overwritten. Only three fixed-shape fields (tool, commandCategory, commandForm) ever leave the reporter per denial; raw commands/paths/prompts/IDs/errors are never included, verified by tests that smuggle a synthetic secret through every untrusted field and assert it never appears in the report, stdout, or stderr. The new workflow steps use `continue-on-error: true` and `if: failure() && steps.model.outcome == 'failure'`, so they only fire on an actual model-step failure, can't themselves flip the job back to success, and are skipped for preflight failures or cancellations — confirmed against factory-cycle.yml/factory-pr-review.yml, which gate on job `.result` unaffected by this addition. No other file (policy.cjs, worker.cjs, controller.cjs, permissions blocks, FACTORY_ENABLED gate, turn-ceiling logic) was touched. The new test file is automatically picked up by the existing `yarn test:factory` glob already run in CI, so no CI wiring changes were needed. Regression coverage is strong: missing/oversized/malformed/symlinked/directory inputs, truncation at 100 denials, PowerShell command classification, exact-vs-with-arguments vs compound/dynamic command forms, and non-overwrite of an existing output file are all exercised.","findings":[]}

The added UserSettingsForm.test.tsx renders the real component and exercises the actual Yup validation schema (no regex duplication), covers accept/reject cases plus a submission test verifying updateUser is called with the typed phone number, and relies only on already-present devDependencies (vitest, @testing-library/react, jest-dom) and the existing vite.config.ts jsdom test setup — no new dependencies. 60.feedback: {"head":"d0cfe4d4af8b362e536316447c6e2f15353ad8bb","verdict":"pass","summary":"The PR fixes the retained-dependency-version blind spot identified in PR #52's review. `inspectUpdate` now classifies every resulting lock entry of an affected package name as removed/added/retained/baseline by actually following changed selectors and reused dependency paths (via `followSelection`, cycle/bounded via a visited-pair set and 500-item limits), so a version that happens to equal a pre-existing baseline copy is no longer able to dodge the advisory check. `queryOsv` folds \"added\" and \"retained\" into the same rejecting bucket while keeping \"baseline\" advisories reported separately as `remainingBaseline`, and `cleared` is only ever derived from removed-side IDs not also present in baseline, so a cleared ID is guaranteed absent from every resulting version (including retained/added, since the function throws before computing the result if either is vulnerable). `validateReport` strictly requires `version: 2` and the new `changed/candidateVersions/cleared/remainingBaseline` shape, and this is reused unmodified by `policy.reserve`/`DependencyMerger`, so historical v1 ledger analysis records remain readable but cannot authorize a new review or premerge (covered by a dedicated regression in factory-dependency-policy.test.cjs that triggers through `policy.reserve`'s `validateReport` call). Evidence collection (`dependency-evidence.cjs`) verifies registry source/integrity and OSV advisory records for all non-removed sides including retained/baseline, with strict parsing and size/count bounds that fail closed on malformed, oversized, or inconsistent data. The yarn.lock patch is minimal and verified: the two previously-separate form-data selectors (`^4.0.0`→4.0.1 and `^4.0.4`/`~4.0.4`→4.0.4) are consolidated into one `form-data@^4.0.0, ^4.0.4, ~4.0.4` entry at 4.0.6, with only the required `hasown` bump (new 2.0.4 entry alongside the untouched 2.0.2 one) and a `mime-types` selector widening that resolves to an already-present 2.1.35 entry; package.json, resolutions, and the private parser-tool lock are untouched. A real regression test exercises the installed `form-data` package for the multipart CRLF header-injection bug directly. Operational boundaries (factory switches false, no workflow/ledger/policy changes, no model invocation) are respected — only dependency-analysis/evidence/run scripts, tests, and docs changed.","findings":[{"severity":"minor","message":"dependency-run.cjs's analyze() path calls queryOsv without details=true and discards osv.packages, so the analysis/premerge CI-bound report only carries changed/candidateVersions/cleared/remainingBaseline (as intended for v2), but relies entirely on dependency-evidence.cjs's separate collectEvidence() call to supply the reviewer with per-package side/advisory detail. This split is consistent with the ticket but worth double-checking in the real workflow wiring (not part of this diff) that both the analysis-stage report and the evidence packet are always produced from the same inventory/queries so they can't diverge."}]}

{"head":"2ab7e7164761a09f580dd0109ccb5aa4c34811ce","verdict":"pass","summary":"This PR prepares (but does not enable) a default-off feed-contract pagination probe and adds verified, evidence-bound incident retirement to the production monitor, per ticket #63. I reviewed the full implementation (app-checks-contract.cjs, app-checks-probe.cjs, app-checks.cjs, monitor.cjs, monitor-recovery.cjs, monitor-recovery-contract.cjs, monitor-state.cjs, monitor-proof.cjs, the factory-monitor.yml workflow) against the diff's file list and the acceptance criteria, plus the associated test suites and docs.

Findings:
- The feed-contract probe (`app-checks-probe.cjs: validFeedContract`) correctly accepts a bounded 400/422 documented rejection or coherent positive bounded pagination (limit 1-50, consistent totalPages/hasNextPages), and rejects 200 responses with null/incoherent metadata, matching the acceptance criterion. It is strictly additive to the existing page=1/limit=5 journey and adds no live request when `FACTORY_FEED_CONTRACT_CHECK_ENABLED` is absent/false (verified by `app-checks-probe.cjs` gating and the "default-off adds no request" test).
- The workflow's `feed_contract`/`app_checks` preview inputs are wired so the override only takes effect when `dry_run=true` (`factory-monitor.yml` env expressions, exercised by `factory-monitor-workflow.test.cjs`), and feed-contract mode cannot be enabled without `FACTORY_APP_CHECKS_ENABLED` (checked in `monitor.cjs:main`).
- Probe-mode binding is enforced end-to-end: reports are versioned 2 only when `feedContract` is present and must match the running mode (`readReport` throws on mismatch); the incident's `probeMode: "feed-contract"` is baked into the immutable proof (`monitor-proof.cjs`) and checked again before any retirement (`observeIncident`'s `required_probe_missing` branch, and `verifyRepair`'s requireProof on `probeMode`/`feedContract === "ok"`/matching release SHAs before and after the journey).
- `monitor-recovery.cjs` verifies real, independently-checkable evidence before closing an issue: ledger ticket status/review/merge, protected-branch CI success, a single successful first-attempt `factory-deploy.yml` run for the exact merge commit with named-owner environment approval, trusted workflow source at both SHAs, and fresh healthy same-mode probes bound to that release. Ambiguous/missing/forged evidence throws and is caught by `monitor.cjs`'s `recovery_held` fallback, which records `recovered` but never closes the issue, matches, edits, or resets counters — this is covered by an extensive test matrix in `factory-monitor-recovery.test.cjs` (malformed/forged provenance, wrong approval/release/deployment, active concurrent work, lost close/final responses, repeated retirement idempotency, legacy vs. feed-contract scope).
- The isolated drill path (`monitor-drill.cjs`) calls `observeIncident` directly without `verifiedRetirement`, so the new verified-closure logic is only reachable from the real `monitor()` flow — the drill boundary is preserved, not weakened.
- No application source (`src/`, `backend/`) was touched; the real `limit=0` defect is only demonstrated (not fixed) via a disposable local Postgres + compiled production-mode app in `production-integration.test.cjs`, consistent with "confirm but don't fix" in the ticket. The verification doc explicitly states no production host, model, or paid API was used during preparation, and the three factory switches (`FACTORY_ENABLED`/`FACTORY_AUTOMATION_ENABLED`/`FACTORY_AUTOMERGE_ENABLED`, in untouched `policy.cjs`) and existing monitor/stop settings are unaffected.
- The operator/evidence runbook (`docs/factory/MONITOR-TO-REPAIR-ACCEPTANCE.md`) is included and matches the implemented controls and budgets (eight-request/206s contract journey vs. 212s standard, fits the existing 8-minute job, confirmed by `phaseBudgets` and a budget-math test).

No critical or important issues found.","findings":[{"severity":"minor","message":"docs/factory/MONITOR-TO-REPAIR-ACCEPTANCE.md line 76 contains a mojibake artifact ("Actions Ã¢â€ â€™ Production monitor Ã¢â€ â€™ Run workflow Ã¢â€ â€™ main"), apparently a double-encoded UTF-8 arrow character (→) saved incorrectly.
